study_design: Case-control study of African-American men with prostate cancer and screening controls
reason: The abstract compares men undergoing treatment for prostate cancer with screening controls and analyzes overall prostate cancer status. It does not report an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: AA men (age 40-70) with normal levels of serum vitD (>30 ng/ml) had a 71% lower risk of PCa compared to AA men with vitD deficiency (OR = 0.29, 95%CI: 0.08-1.03; P = 0.055).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns overall prostate cancer status rather than aggressive disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In individuals with vitD deficiency, increased dietary quercetin showed a tendency toward lower risk of PCa (OR = 0.91, 95%CI: 0.82-1.00; P = 0.054, age-adjusted) while men with normal vitD were at elevated risk (OR = 1.23, 95%CI: 1.04-1.45).
estimate_classifications.reason: The quercetin estimate is for overall prostate cancer among vitamin D-deficient men, not an aggressive endpoint.
